answer: A sequential delay defence makes each identity pay in unforgeable time. Before any paid job, an agent must solve a verifiable delay puzzle bound to its public key, a computation that cannot be parallelised, like a terrace built one stone at a time. A Sybil operator with a saffron field of fake names gains nothing from more machines: every extra identity needs its own sequential delay, so the cost of one more fake is a full delay, not a fraction. The pigment of honest work is the completed delay itself, publicly checkable in milliseconds, and identities that skip it earn nothing.
